newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mayflower to boost U.S. car market presence.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mayflower to boost U.S. car market presence.

text.p: One of Britain's up and coming auto engineering companies, Mayflower Plc, will drive up its share of the lucrative U.S. car market after a $165 million buy of metal pressing supplier SCSM Holdings unveiled on Thursday.

Mayflower has made big inroads recently into the market for supplying major manufacturers with complete body shells for low volume cars -- including the MG sports car for BMW AG and Chrysler's new Plymouth Prowler hot-rod.
Finance director David Donnelly told Reuters the planned buy of private SCSM would make Mayflower the fourth biggest independent stamping company in the United States.
It would also enhance Mayflower's earnings and cash flow immediately and improve its profitability, he said.

He added that the agreement to pay $137.2 million for the privately-owned company, and take up debt of $27.8 million, was watertight and could not be spoiled by a rival bidder -- unlike Mayflower's failed 172 million pound ($282.3 million) bid this year for Pullman/Clevite, pipped by Tenneco Inc.
"The deal is only subject to our shareholders' approval; nobody else can come in," Donnelly told Reuters by telephone.
The initial response to the deal from the share market was positive with the company's shares trading were up nine pence, or 6.7 percent, at 144p at 1400 GMT in heavy volume.
While the SCSM deal is smaller in value than the proposed Clevite purchase, Donnelly said it provided a better fit.
"I would say in strategic terms it is more significant because it fits very nicely into what we're already doing."
Buying Clevite would have allowed Mayflower to diversify from body pressings into suspension systems
He saw SCSM and Mayflower together making U.S. sales worth some $300 million next year, compared with enlarged total group turnover of about 400 million pounds ($656.5 million).
The merger would unite two complementary sets of U.S. customers as well as linking two different structural specialities, Donnelly added.

While SCSM does a lot of work on complex inner panels for car companies, especially for pick-ups and light utility vehicles, Mayflower's bread and butter in the U.S. is so-called outer panel work for truck manufacturers.
The combination should allow the enlarged group to seek new contracts supplying whole bodyshells, and so-called "major sub- assemblies" at a time when the market for such work is growing.

Donnelly said he anticipated the group being able to win work on programmes such as the new Mercedes-Benz sport utility which is set to go into U.S. production in 1997 and for which SCSM will supply about half of the pressed components.

Mayflower was confident of being well-placed to win more business in the U.S., even though it will not be biggest in its market, because it also has experience of a wide range of materials and a strong base of specialist design skills.

The British group has already lined up financing for the acquisition which will be partly supported by a placing and open offer 32.83 million new shares at 126 pence each which it expects will raise 38.2 million pounds ($62.91 million).
Mayflower intends to hold an extraordinary meeting on December 2, to seek shareholder approval for the deal.
